<action type="say">
Here are the basic steps that work for almost any airline:

1) Find the booking  
- Open your email and search for words like “Your trip”, “Itinerary”, “Confirmation”, or “E‑ticket” around the time you booked.  
- Open the email and click “Manage trip”, “View reservation”, or similar (this takes you to the airline’s site/app with your booking loaded).  
- If you don’t see a link, go to the airline’s website/app, look for “My trips” or “Manage booking”, and enter:  
  - Confirmation code, and  
  - Last name.

2) See refund/fees before cancelling  
Once you’re on the trip details page, look for one of:  
- “Cancel flight”, “Change/Cancel”, or “Refund options”.  
Click that, but don’t confirm yet. The next screen usually shows:  
- Whether your ticket is refundable or nonrefundable.  
- If you’ll get:  
  - Money back to your card, or  
  - Flight/travel credit only.  
- Any cancellation fee and the final refund/credit amount.

3) Decide and confirm cancellation  
- If the amount/refund type looks acceptable, proceed with “Confirm cancellation” / “Yes, cancel”.  
- Save or screenshot the:  
  - Cancellation confirmation number, and  
  - Refund/credit amount and type (cash vs credit) and expiry date if it’s a credit.

If you tell me what you see on that “Cancel” or “Refund” screen (e.g., “You’ll receive a $X travel credit, nonrefundable”), I can interpret it for you and confirm what you’re giving up/keeping before you click the final button.</action>
